sections.content: Content includes concepts and theories related to decision making. Lots of real world examples are used to support the lessons. Later in the sem it will dive more into the quantitative analysis portion of making decisions. Overall, the content seems interesting and the class uses a lot of examples.
sections.teaching: Professor is very nice and friendly and encourages you to speak in class. Sometimes he will lecture and uses a lot of real world examples to explain concepts, which is helpful. You do need to pay attention in class and take notes though because he just talks about concepts on the spot, but the lecture is also recorded so it's not too stressful. He uses a flipped classroom model sometimes so class will be more focused on discussion rather than lecturing.
sections.grading: The grading consists of midterm, final, weekly review, quiz, and participation. You do need to show up to class and say some things in class for participation. Other than that, grading is straightfoward and clear.
sections.workload: Workload is reasonable. Weekly readings and recorded lectures are watched before class, and also weekly quiz on the content.

sections.content:
Check other reviews for the full syllabus.
Could be interesting, some of them are on recent issues such as Corona. Lots of real life examples to aid the concept explanation.

BUT half the contents are quantitative including probability, stats and hypothesis testing so if you don't like math (like me), might wanna consider other SA SSC. If you took ISOM2700 with him, some contents are exactly the same (cakes, shadow price, EOQ)
If you're good at excel, you're already halfway there.
sections.teaching:
Pretty good teaching; he goes through everything step by step. He always brings up various real life examples.
Also, very clear and plain English which is a rare find in UST. Some complained he has Indian accent and they can't understand him but I think his English is darn good compared to some local or mainland profs. (maybe since he lived in the States for a while and worked at McKinsey?) He speaks slowly for everyone to follow, so you can just put it on 1.5x or stuff.
sections.grading:
He said absolute grading on the syllabus but not sure how they graded us at the end.
I got 1sd above mean for the midterm and 0.5sd above mean for the final which account for 70% of the grade. For the group project, I got a full mark - make sure you find good groupmates.
We had participation from leaving comments during the zoom lecture - you don't have to speak up, just leave your cam on and answer to his questions through the chat function.
You have weekly quizzes on Canvas and you get 2 chances so everyone would get full marks here.
I got an A at the end and for an SSC, I think the grading is generous.
sections.workload:
Not too much; short weekly quizzes, 1 real time zoom lecture and 1 weekly youtube lectures to watch with one group project.
But contents-wise, there are quite a lot to learn so if you don't follow with contents every week, you might die towards the end of the sem (finals) cuz you realize you actually have a lot to learn.
If you did stats options in IB HL Maths, you'll have even less workload.

sections.grading:
See others for rubrics.

For my grading, I got A with the following marks:
Midterm: 33/35
Final: 40/45
Group project: 10/10
Attendance/ in-class quizzes/ Assignment: Idk, I only miss one attendance and late submit one assignment. Not a big issue at all.

One thing is that he did not allow you to go back in the online exam (you cannot change your answer once you click next question). That made me a little worried at first.

His final exam is tricky. Changing 1-2 numbers in similar questions. Just make sure you stay calm, active your "System 2" thinking, all would be fine!
sections.workload:
Just attendance and some assignments. The attendance is just simple quizzes and the assignment is just copying what he did in the lecture. If you are a normal person, you will get all marks.

Group Project: if you devote 2 days into it, you end up with full mark easily.

Light Workload overall.

sections.content: The range of content is wide enough to cover everything from excel using to AR/VR. The context is just too wide and shallow, a lot the content is repeating and meaningless. Sometimes reading the context is difficult and miserable as the sentences are very long and containing a lot of ''which'', "by referring"..... to be simple, hard to read. As for the content itself, a lot but meaningless, difficult to look for key point to revise.
sections.teaching: Teaching was really poor. This course basically expected you to self-learning but actually teaching you anything. Professor always said, my friend did you read the context on canvas my friend? He literally expected you to understand the content and he will simply brief you through it during the lesson. Plus his English is too terrible, any P.6 student is better than him. Impossible to listen to conclude.
